newsitem.title: USA: Monsanto up on short-term earnings outlook.
newsitem.headline: Monsanto up on short-term earnings outlook.

text.p: Shares of Monsanto Co rose on Friday after the company indicated to investors and analysts earlier this week that its long-term growth objectives would not hamper short-term earnings, analysts said.
The stock was 1-5/8 higher at 37-3/8 by early afternoon.

"...The company's management understands that premium price-earnings ratios are assigned to companies that deliver consistent financial performance and earnings growth on a year-to-year basis, as well as create the prospect for superior growth over a longer-term horizon," Monsanto said in a report issued this week on First Call.
Analysts said Monsanto's statement was interpreted as indicating the company would meet short-term earnings targets.

Nicholas Filippello, chief economist for St. Louis-based Monsanto, declined to comment specifically on the First Call consensus estimate that the company would earn $0.53 a share in the first quarter, compared with earnings of $0.45 a share in the year-earlier period.

Asked why Monsanto issued the statement, Filippello said, "The stock had been under some downward pressure, and there has been some concern among analysts and some investors that perhaps Monsanto had shifted its balance between short-term performance and long-term performance."
"We think we can do both," he added.

In an interview last month, Filippello said Monsanto likely would increase its spending on new businesses, product development and other investments in 1997. In 1996, that spending rose by about $350 million around $900 million.
Monsanto is an agriculture, pharmaceutical and food ingredient company.
